title: A lisse E sheaf has a constructible integral lattice
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$ and $A_T(V)=C(|V|,A)$ for the sheaves of continuous functions with pointwise ring operations and restriction by precomposition, so $A_T$ is the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $L$ be an $E_T$-module sheaf which is pro-etale locally free of finite rank. There is an $A_T$-module sheaf $N$, and an isomorphism $E_T\otimes_{A_T}N\cong L$, such that $N$ admits a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on every stratum of which it is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A P$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $P$. The tensor product is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The assertion requires only a constructible integral sheaf; it does not require $N$ to be locally free on all of $T$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], the rings in the statement are precisely the completed integral and continuous rational coefficient sheaves, $E_T=A_T[1/\varpi]$, and restriction to any locally closed subscheme identifies the two coefficient rings with the corresponding rings there. Write $S(M)=E_T\otimes_{A_T}M=M[1/\varpi]$. As an underlying abelian sheaf this is the filtered colimit of $M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$: the class of $m$ at stage $n$ is $m/\varpi^n$, and the transition relation is precisely the fraction relation. The two colimit nodes identify module colimits with the underlying abelian colimits and make this functor exact. Restriction of scalars from $E_T$ to $A_T$ is exact because kernels and cokernels have their underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2; setup for the final paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13

proof.text: For constructible integral sheaves $P,Q$ as in the statement, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] puts $P[0],Q[0]$ in the bounded constructible complete category. Scalar extension $S$ is left adjoint to restriction of scalars $U$: the adjunction sends $\phi$ to $m\mapsto\phi(1\otimes m)$, with inverse $\psi\mapsto(e\otimes m\mapsto e\psi(m))$. Both functors are exact by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to identify their derived functors with termwise application. The derived adjunction [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] consequently gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E_T)}(S(P),S(Q)[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_T)}(P,U S(Q)[1])$. The essential-constancy requirements of that node hold because exact functors invert every quasi-isomorphism, so all objects in each resolution diagram map isomorphically to its value on the original complex.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Ext formula in the last paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13; expanded using Stacks Tags 0949, 0CRK, 094A and 08JA.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] to the sequence of $A_T$-module complexes $Q[0][1]\xrightarrow{\varpi}Q[0][1]\to\cdots$. Its termwise colimit is $U S(Q)[1]$ by step 1. Thus, with $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}Q[1]$ and $s\iota_n=\iota_{n+1}\varpi$, there is the distinguished telescope triangle $B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to U S(Q)[1]\to B[1]$. The cited node supplies both the derived coproduct universal property and the cone-to-colimit quasi-isomorphism; the transition maps need not be injective.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Ext formula in the last paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13; expanded using Stacks Tags 0949, 0CRK, 094A and 08JA.

proof.text: We identify the cohomology of global derived Hom with derived morphisms. For any $M$ and integer $r$, [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-right] identifies $R\mathcal Hom(P,M)[r]$ with $R\mathcal Hom(P,M[r])$. Derived sections commute with this shift: a K-injective resolution $I$ can be shifted by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], and termwise sections give $\Gamma(I[r])=\Gamma(I)[r]$. Taking $H^0$ and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] therefore yields the natural identification $H^r R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_T}(P,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_T)}(P,M[r])$. This uses global derived Hom as defined in [def-weil-pbc-adic-global-derived-hom], not sheaf-valued internal Hom.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Ext formula in the last paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13; expanded using Stacks Tags 0949, 0CRK, 094A and 08JA.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-bounded-below-compactness] to the copies of $Q[1]$ and to the copies of $Q[2]$. Each family has a common lower cohomological bound, respectively $-1$ and $-2$; no global compactness in the unbounded derived category is claimed. Taking degree zero and using the preceding identification gives the two bijections $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,B)$ and $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,B[1])$. To take degree zero of the coproduct of $A$-module complexes, use [lem-kun-derived-countable-sums-exact]: termwise sums represent derived sums. Their cohomology is the sum of the cohomologies, since exact sums preserve the short exact sequences defining cycles, boundaries and the quotients of cycles by boundaries. The shift $[1]$ preserves coproducts because its inverse is $[-1]$, identifying the second target with the indicated $B[1]$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Ext formula in the last paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13; expanded using Stacks Tags 0949, 0CRK, 094A and 08JA.

proof.text:
The preceding two comparisons are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-sequence-relative-hom-telescope] for $K=P[0]$ and $X_n=Q[0][1]$. Apply it to the telescope above, then use the derived adjunction and [def-pc-ext], to obtain
$$\varinjlim\bigl(\operatorname{Ext}^1_{A_T}(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\varpi}\operatorname{Ext}^1_{A_T}(P,Q)\to\cdots\bigr)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_{E_T}(S(P),S(Q)).$$
The left side is $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{A_T}(P,Q)[1/\varpi]$: $\alpha$ at stage $n$ maps to $\alpha/\varpi^n$ and the colimit relation is the fraction relation. For a class $\alpha:P\to Q[1]$, the stage-zero morphism is $\eta_Q[1]\alpha$ for the localization unit $\eta_Q:Q\to U S(Q)$; the adjunction identifies it with $S(\alpha)$. If $a_n$ is the stage-$n$ map, the colimit relation gives $\varpi a_{n+1}=a_n$. Multiplication by $\varpi$ is invertible on $U S(Q)$, so $a_n=\varpi^{-n}a_0$. In particular every rational extension class is $S(\alpha)/\varpi^n$ for an integral class $\alpha$ and $n\geq0$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Ext formula in the last paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13; expanded using Stacks Tags 0949, 0CRK, 094A and 08JA.

proof.text: Consequently the rationalizations of constructible integral sheaves are closed under extensions. Given $0\to S(Q)\to F\to S(P)\to0$, let its class be $S(\alpha)/\varpi^n$ as in step 6. Degree-one extension classification realizes $\alpha$ by $0\to Q\to N\to P\to0$. The short-exact-complex triangle node identifies its middle term with the shifted cone of its connecting morphism. The integral characterization then makes $N$ constructible: its degree-zero complex is the shifted cone of $P[0]\xrightarrow{\alpha}Q[0][1]$, hence belongs to the integral category, and clause (iii) describes its cohomology $N$. Exact scalar extension sends this sequence to the class $S(\alpha)$. Pushing its rational sequence out along the automorphism $\varpi^{-n}$ of $S(Q)$ changes its class to $S(\alpha)/\varpi^n$; because this is an automorphism, its middle term is isomorphic to $S(N)$. The bijection in extension classification now identifies that sequence with the given sequence, so $S(N)\cong F$. This is only an isomorphism of middle terms, as required; the chosen identification of the subobject has been scaled.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, last paragraph; Stacks Tag 06XV (lemma-ext-1) for extension classification

proof.text: We prove the assertion for every reduced closed subscheme $X$ of $T$, and every lisse $E_X$-sheaf, by noetherian induction on its closed support. Such $X$ is noetherian, finite-dimensional and $\ell$-coprime: affine rings are quotients of noetherian rings, strict chains of closed irreducible subsets are chains in $T$, and an inverse of $\ell$ maps to an inverse in every quotient local ring. The minimal-closed-subset node supplies the induction, with empty support having the zero model. On a nonempty reduced $X$, use [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-etale-local] to obtain an etale covering with lisse integral models. Choose a finite affine Zariski covering of $X$ and apply etale affine refinement on each affine; the resulting finite disjoint union $Y$ of affine schemes is a jointly surjective etale cover carrying a lisse integral model. Both $X$ and $Y$ are qcqs: $X$ is noetherian, and $Y$ is a finite union of affine components. Apply etale stratified finiteness to $Y\to X$. On each stratum the pullback is finite etale and surjective and the integral model pulls back to a lisse integral model. The coefficient restriction of step 1 identifies these as the required coefficient sheaves. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-finite-etale-descent] gives a lisse integral model for the restriction of $L$ to each of these strata.

Extract a nonempty open $U\subseteq X$ on which such a model exists. There are finitely many irreducible components, each with a generic point. Choose a component $C$ and its generic point $\eta$, and the stratum $Z\hookrightarrow X$ containing $\eta$. Write its image as $O\cap F$ with $O$ open and $F$ closed. Since $F$ contains $\eta$, it contains $C$. Remove all other components and intersect with $O$. The resulting nonempty open $U$ lies in $C\cap O$, hence in the image of $Z$. It factors through $Z$ as a scheme: in the open part of the stratum immersion its ideal sections vanish at every point of the reduced open subscheme $U$, so lie in its nilradical and are zero. On affine charts this is exactly factorization of the ring map through the quotient defining the closed immersion. Pull back the stratum model along this open immersion $U\to Z$ to get a lisse integral model $M_U$ of $L|_U$. The open is quasi-compact by the noetherian-open node.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, passage from a finite stratification to a constructible filtration; explicit reduced-scheme dense-open argument

proof.text: Let $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme of $X\setminus U$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the open immersion. Its support is strictly smaller. The induction hypothesis supplies a constructible integral model $M_Z$ for $i^{-1}L$. Put $Q=j_!M_U$ and $P=i_*M_Z$. The ringed open-closed node gives their restrictions $(M_U,0)$ and $(0,M_Z)$ on $U,Z_0$. Consequently adjoining the open stratum $U$ to the finitely many strata of $Z_0$ proves both $P$ and $Q$ are constructible integral sheaves. The local modules are finite free on $U$ and the given finitely presented modules on $Z_0$, with zero modules on the complementary pieces. Scalar localization commutes with $i_*$ because that node gives filtered-colimit preservation for qcqs $X$. It commutes with $j_!$ because $j_!$ is a left adjoint, hence preserves the sequential colimit expressing localization; the scalar multiplications and the coefficient identifications in step 1 identify these colimits as module sheaves. Therefore $S(Q)\cong j_!j^{-1}L$ and $S(P)\cong i_*i^{-1}L$. The same node gives $0\to S(Q)\to L\to S(P)\to0$. Step 7 now provides a constructible integral model for $L$ on $X$, completing the noetherian induction.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, last paragraph; Stacks Tags 09AA, 09AH, 09BN and 03DI for open-closed assembly

proof.text: Finally let $r:T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow T$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme with full support. The open-closed node applied with empty complementary open gives $L\cong r_*r^{-1}L$ and $r^{-1}r_*\cong1$. By step 1 its coefficient inverse images are $A_{T_{\mathrm{red}}}$ and $E_{T_{\mathrm{red}}}$. The preceding induction supplies a constructible integral model $N_{\mathrm{red}}$ on $T_{\mathrm{red}}$. Set $N=r_*N_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its supporting strata, composed with $r$, are immersions into $T$, partition the same underlying space, and restrict $N$ to the corresponding restrictions of $N_{\mathrm{red}}$ by $r^{-1}r_*\cong1$. Hence they witness precisely the finite stratification required in the statement. Filtered-colimit preservation by $r_*$ gives $S(N)\cong r_*S(N_{\mathrm{red}})\cong r_*r^{-1}L\cong L$. This also covers the empty scheme, rank zero, disconnected schemes and nonreduced schemes, and asserts no global lissity of $N$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_constructible_integral_lattice (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T] (_hdim : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim T ≤ d) (_hℓ : ∀ x : T, IsUnit (l : T.presheaf.stalk x)) (L : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (latticeModuleRing T (WithAbs (Padic.coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue l E)))) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (latticeModuleRing T (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E)), IsContinuousConstructible T (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E) N ∧ Nonempty (SheafOfModules.changeOfRings.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (integralLatticeCoefficientMap T l E) N ≅ L)
lean.note: Uses the canonical continuous coefficient sheaves and valuation topology of the landed lattice-coefficient interface. Constructibility is stratumwise, and no global locally-free hypothesis is imposed on N. Maintainer fix: IsNoetherian T bundles exactly the original locally-noetherian and compact hypotheses and supplies the topologically-noetherian instance for the source-scoped constructibility predicate.
